svg.title: Annualization sanity check from daily to annual sigma
svg.desc: A two-part diagram: the upper part is a transformation pipeline showing daily_sigma of 0.01 multiplied by the square root of 252 trading days per year giving an annualization factor of approximately 15.87 producing an expected annual sigma of approximately 0.159; the lower part is a number line spanning 0.00 to 0.25 with a teal-shaded tolerance band covering 0.10 to 0.25 and a coral tick mark at 0.159 representing the theoretical value, illustrating that the test allows any empirical mean within the wide tolerance band as a pass.
svg.text: Annualization sanity check — does empirical mean land near 0.159?
Why √252? Variance scales linearly with time; standard deviation scales as the square root.
Why the wide tolerance? 100 days of synthetic data carries finite-sample noise.
The empirical mean sits near 0.159 — anywhere in [0.10, 0.25] passes the test.
If the function forgets the √252 multiplier, the result lands near 0.01 — far below 0.10 — and the test fails loudly.
